percent.intro: Percentage Calculator, worked end to end. The calculator takes Percentage, Of this number; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
percent.outro: Percentage Calculator settles it with Percentage of a number = Number × Percentage ÷ 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
percent.hi_intro: Percentage Calculator ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Percentage aur Of this number; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
percent.hi_outro: Percentage Calculator ka formula: Number ka percentage = Number × Percentage ÷ 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

simpleint.intro: Simple Interest, worked end to end. The calculator takes Amount (Principal), Interest Rate, Time; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
simpleint.outro: Simple Interest settles it with Interest = Principal x Rate x Time / 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
simpleint.hi_intro: Simple Interest ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Amount (Principal) aur Interest Rate aur Time; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
simpleint.hi_outro: Simple Interest ka formula: Interest = Principal x Rate x Time / 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

compint.intro: Compound Interest, worked end to end. The calculator takes Amount (Principal), Interest Rate, Time, Times compounded per year; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
compint.outro: Compound Interest settles it with Total = Principal × (1 + Rate ÷ Times ÷ 100) ^ (Times × Years). Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
compint.hi_intro: Compound Interest ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Amount (Principal) aur Interest Rate aur Time aur Times compounded per year; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
compint.hi_outro: Compound Interest ka formula: Total = Principal × (1 + Rate ÷ Times ÷ 100) ^ (Times × Years). Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

emi.intro: A ₹10,00,000 loan at 8% for five years — a typical car or personal loan, not a mortgage. Here is the instalment the lender will quote.
emi.outro: The EMI is ₹20,276 and the interest over the five years is ₹2,16,584 — about a fifth of the loan. Push the same loan out to twenty years and the EMI halves to ₹8,364, but the interest crosses ₹10,00,000. That gap is why the term is entered in months and the total is watched, not just the instalment.
emi.hi_intro: Loan EMI Calculator ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Loan Amount aur Interest Rate aur Loan Tenure; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
emi.hi_outro: Loan EMI Calculator ka formula: EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n − 1), jahan P Loan Amount hai, r monthly rate (Interest Rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100) aur n Loan Tenure mahine mein. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

savegoal.intro: Say you want ₹5,00,000, you already have ₹1,00,000, and you can put aside ₹15,000 a month.
savegoal.outro: Change the monthly amount above and the time to the goal moves with it. Even a small increase, held for years, moves the date a long way.
savegoal.hi_intro: Savings Goal Planner ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Savings Goal aur Already Saved aur Saved Each Month; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
savegoal.hi_outro: Savings Goal Planner ka formula: Mahine = (Goal minus ab tak bachaya) ÷ har mahine bachaya jaane wala amount. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

takehome.intro: Salary Take-Home Estimator, worked end to end. The calculator takes Annual CTC, Estimated Deductions; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
takehome.outro: Salary Take-Home Estimator settles it with Take-home = Gross Salary - Employee PF (12% of basic) - Professional Tax - TDS. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
takehome.hi_intro: Salary Take-Home Estimator ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Annual CTC aur Estimated Deductions; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
takehome.hi_outro: Salary Take-Home Estimator ka formula: Take-home = Gross Salary - Employee PF (basic ka 12%) - Professional Tax - TDS. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

numwords.intro: Type a figure and the tool writes it the way an Indian cheque expects.
numwords.outro: Always check the words against the digits before you sign. A mismatch is what causes a payment to be held up.
numwords.hi_intro: Number to Words (Indian) ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Number; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
numwords.hi_outro: Number to Words (Indian) ka formula: Indian grouping right se teen digit ke blocks mein hoti hai - pehle hazaar, phir lakh, phir crore. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

gross.intro: Gross Profit & Margin, worked end to end. The calculator takes Total Revenue, Cost of Goods Sold; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
gross.outro: Gross Profit & Margin settles it with Gross Profit = Revenue − Cost of Goods Sold, so ₹10,00,000 − ₹6,00,000 = ₹4,00,000. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
gross.hi_intro: Gross Profit & Margin ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Total Revenue aur Cost of Goods Sold; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
gross.hi_outro: Gross Profit & Margin ka formula: Gross Profit = Revenue − Cost of Goods Sold, yaani ₹10,00,000 − ₹6,00,000 = ₹4,00,000. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

ebitda.intro: EBITDA & Margin, worked end to end. The calculator takes Revenue, Cost of Goods Sold, Operating Expenses; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
ebitda.outro: EBITDA & Margin settles it with EBITDA = Revenue − Cost of Goods Sold − Operating Expenses. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
ebitda.hi_intro: EBITDA & Margin ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Revenue aur Cost of Goods Sold aur Operating Expenses; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
ebitda.hi_outro: EBITDA & Margin ka formula: EBITDA = Revenue − Cost of Goods Sold − Operating Expenses. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

opmargin.intro: Operating Margin, worked end to end. The calculator takes Revenue, Operating Profit; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
opmargin.outro: Operating Margin settles it with Operating Margin = Operating Profit ÷ Revenue × 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
opmargin.hi_intro: Operating Margin ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Revenue aur Operating Profit; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
opmargin.hi_outro: Operating Margin ka formula: Operating Margin = Operating Profit ÷ Revenue × 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

netmargin.intro: Take a business with ₹4,50,000 of revenue that keeps ₹1,80,000 after every cost and tax. Here is the net margin.
netmargin.outro: 40% is a strong net margin for most trades. If your figure is much lower, the leak is below the gross line — look at overheads, interest and tax before you look at price.
netmargin.hi_intro: Net Profit Margin ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Revenue aur Net Profit; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
netmargin.hi_outro: Net Profit Margin ka formula: Net margin = net profit ÷ revenue × 100 (`np` ÷ `rev` × 100). Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

cm.intro: Contribution Margin, worked end to end. The calculator takes Selling Price / Unit, Variable Cost / Unit; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
cm.outro: Contribution Margin settles it with Contribution margin per unit = selling price - variable cost per unit. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
cm.hi_intro: Contribution Margin ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Selling Price / Unit aur Variable Cost / Unit; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
cm.hi_outro: Contribution Margin ka formula: Contribution margin per unit = selling price - variable cost per unit. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

markup.intro: Markup vs Margin, worked end to end. The calculator takes Cost Price, Selling Price; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
markup.outro: Markup vs Margin settles it with Markup % = (Selling Price − Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price × 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
markup.hi_intro: Markup vs Margin ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Cost Price aur Selling Price; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
markup.hi_outro: Markup vs Margin ka formula: Markup % = (Selling Price − Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price × 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

roi.intro: Return on Investment (ROI), worked end to end. The calculator takes Net Profit, Investment Cost; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
roi.outro: Return on Investment (ROI) settles it with ROI is net profit divided by investment cost, times 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
roi.hi_intro: Return on Investment (ROI) ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Net Profit aur Investment Cost; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
roi.hi_outro: Return on Investment (ROI) ka formula: ROI = net profit / investment cost x 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

roce.intro: Return on Capital Employed, worked end to end. The calculator takes Operating Profit, Capital Employed; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
roce.outro: Return on Capital Employed settles it with ROCE is operating profit (EBIT) divided by capital employed, times 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
roce.hi_intro: Return on Capital Employed ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Operating Profit aur Capital Employed; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
roce.hi_outro: Return on Capital Employed ka formula: ROCE = operating profit (EBIT) / capital employed x 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

impval.intro: Say a founder is offered ₹10,00,000 for 10% of the business. The two numbers look small next to each other; implied valuation turns them into the one figure the round is really about — the price they put on the whole company.
impval.outro: At ₹10,00,000 for 10%, the cheque implies a ₹1,00,00,000 company. Offer the same ₹10,00,000 for 5% instead and the implied price doubles; change either field above and the whole-company value moves with it.
impval.hi_intro: Maano ek founder ko business ke 10% ke liye ₹10,00,000 ka offer milta hai. Do chhote numbers lagte hain, par implied valuation inhi ko ek price bana deta hai — poori company ki value jo round ka asli sawaal hai.
impval.hi_outro: ₹10,00,000 me 10% ka matlab ₹1,00,00,000 ki company. Wahi cheque 5% ke liye do to implied price dugna ho jaata hai; upar koi bhi field badlo aur poori company ki value saath badalti hai.

prepost.intro: A term sheet names a ₹90,00,000 pre-money and a ₹10,00,000 cheque. Neither number on its own says what the investor ends up owning; the post-money does, and it is the sum of the two.
prepost.outro: The ₹10,00,000 cheque on a ₹90,00,000 pre-money makes a ₹1,00,00,000 company and hands over 10%. Raise the cheque without moving the pre-money and the stake grows; change either field above to see the split.
prepost.hi_intro: Term sheet me ₹90,00,000 pre-money aur ₹10,00,000 ka cheque likha hai. Ye do numbers akele nahi batate investor ka hissa kitna hoga; post-money batata hai, aur wo dono ka jod hai.
prepost.hi_outro: ₹90,00,000 pre-money par ₹10,00,000 ka cheque ₹1,00,00,000 ki company banata hai aur 10% deta hai. Pre-money badle bina cheque badhao to stake badh jaata hai; upar koi bhi field badlo aur hissa dekho.

revmul.intro: Revenue Multiple, worked end to end. The calculator takes Valuation, Annual Revenue; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
revmul.outro: Revenue Multiple settles it with Revenue Multiple = Valuation ÷ Annual Revenue. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
revmul.hi_intro: Revenue Multiple ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Valuation aur Annual Revenue; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
revmul.hi_outro: Revenue Multiple ka formula: Revenue Multiple = Valuation ÷ Annual Revenue. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

ebitdamul.intro: EBITDA Multiple, worked end to end. The calculator takes Valuation, EBITDA; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
ebitdamul.outro: EBITDA Multiple settles it with EBITDA Multiple = Valuation ÷ EBITDA. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
ebitdamul.hi_intro: EBITDA Multiple ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Valuation aur EBITDA; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
ebitdamul.hi_outro: EBITDA Multiple ka formula: EBITDA Multiple = Valuation ÷ EBITDA. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

dilution.intro: Dilution Calculator, worked end to end. The calculator takes Founder Equity (Before), Equity Offered in This Deal; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
dilution.outro: Dilution Calculator settles it with Founder Equity After = Founder Equity Before − Equity Offered. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
dilution.hi_intro: Dilution Calculator ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Founder Equity (Before) aur Equity Offered in This Deal; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
dilution.hi_outro: Dilution Calculator ka formula: Founder Equity After = Founder Equity Before − Equity Offered. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

ask.intro: Ask Calculator, worked end to end. The calculator takes Amount Needed, Your Believed Valuation; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
ask.outro: Ask Calculator settles it with Equity to Offer = Amount Needed ÷ Valuation × 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
ask.hi_intro: Ask Calculator ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Amount Needed aur Your Believed Valuation; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
ask.hi_outro: Ask Calculator ka formula: Equity to Offer = Amount Needed ÷ Valuation × 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

debteq.intro: Debt + Equity Deal, worked end to end. The calculator takes Total Deal Amount, Debt Portion, Valuation (for equity part); the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
debteq.outro: Debt + Equity Deal settles it with Debt Amount = Total Deal × Debt Portion %; Equity Amount = Total Deal − Debt Amount; Equity % = Equity Amount ÷ Valuation × 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
debteq.hi_intro: Debt + Equity Deal ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Total Deal Amount aur Debt Portion aur Valuation (for equity part); neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
debteq.hi_outro: Debt + Equity Deal ka formula: Debt Amount = Total Deal × Debt Portion %; Equity Amount = Total Deal − Debt Amount; Equity % = Equity Amount ÷ Valuation × 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

royalty.intro: Royalty Deal, worked end to end. The calculator takes Investment Amount, Royalty Rate, Expected Annual Revenue; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
royalty.outro: Royalty Deal settles it with Annual Royalty = Expected Annual Revenue × Royalty Rate %; Payback Period (years) = Investment ÷ Annual Royalty. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
royalty.hi_intro: Royalty Deal ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Investment Amount aur Royalty Rate aur Expected Annual Revenue; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
royalty.hi_outro: Royalty Deal ka formula: Annual Royalty = Expected Annual Revenue × Royalty Rate %; Payback Period (years) = Investment ÷ Annual Royalty. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

captable.intro: Cap Table & ESOP Pool, worked end to end. The calculator takes ESOP Pool, Investor Equity; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
captable.outro: Cap Table & ESOP Pool settles it with Founders' Share = 100% − ESOP Pool − Investor Equity (and any other reserved stake). Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
captable.hi_intro: Cap Table & ESOP Pool ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai ESOP Pool aur Investor Equity; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
captable.hi_outro: Cap Table & ESOP Pool ka formula: Founders' Share = 100% − ESOP Pool − Investor Equity (aur koi bhi reserved hissa). Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

cofounder.intro: Co-founder Equity Split, worked end to end. The calculator takes Founder A Score, Founder B Score, Founder C Score (optional); the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
cofounder.outro: Co-founder Equity Split settles it with Founder Share % = Founder Score ÷ Total of All Scores × 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
cofounder.hi_intro: Co-founder Equity Split ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Founder A Score aur Founder B Score aur Founder C Score (optional); neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
cofounder.hi_outro: Co-founder Equity Split ka formula: Founder Share % = Founder Score ÷ Total of All Scores × 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

dscr.intro: Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR), worked end to end. The calculator takes Net Operating Income (yearly), Total Debt Service (yearly); the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
dscr.outro: Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) settles it with DSCR = Net Operating Income / Total Debt Service, both for the same year. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
dscr.hi_intro: Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Net Operating Income (yearly) aur Total Debt Service (yearly); neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
dscr.hi_outro: Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) ka formula: DSCR = Net Operating Income / Total Debt Service, dono usi saal ke. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

cac.intro: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), worked end to end. The calculator takes Total Sales + Marketing Spend, New Customers; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
cac.outro: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) settles it with CAC = Total Sales and Marketing Spend ÷ New Customers Won. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
cac.hi_intro: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Total Sales + Marketing Spend aur New Customers; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
cac.hi_outro: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) ka formula: CAC = Total Sales aur Marketing Kharch ÷ Naye Customers. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

ltv.intro: Customer Lifetime Value (LTV), worked end to end. The calculator takes Average Order Value, Purchases per Year, Customer Lifespan, Gross Margin; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
ltv.outro: Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) settles it with LTV = Average Order Value × Purchases per Year × Customer Lifespan (years) × Gross Margin %. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
ltv.hi_intro: Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Average Order Value aur Purchases per Year aur Customer Lifespan aur Gross Margin; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
ltv.hi_outro: Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) ka formula: LTV = Average Order Value × Saal me Purchases × Customer Lifespan (saal) × Gross Margin %. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

ltvcac.intro: LTV : CAC Ratio, worked end to end. The calculator takes LTV, CAC; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
ltvcac.outro: LTV : CAC Ratio settles it with LTV : CAC = Customer Lifetime Value ÷ Customer Acquisition Cost. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
ltvcac.hi_intro: LTV : CAC Ratio ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai LTV aur CAC; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
ltvcac.hi_outro: LTV : CAC Ratio ka formula: LTV : CAC = Customer Lifetime Value ÷ Customer Acquisition Cost. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

payback.intro: CAC Payback Period, worked end to end. The calculator takes CAC, Avg Monthly Revenue / Customer, Gross Margin; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
payback.outro: CAC Payback Period settles it with Payback Period (months) = CAC ÷ (Monthly Revenue per Customer × Gross Margin %). Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
payback.hi_intro: CAC Payback Period ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai CAC aur Avg Monthly Revenue / Customer aur Gross Margin; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
payback.hi_outro: CAC Payback Period ka formula: Payback Period (months) = CAC ÷ (Monthly Revenue per Customer × Gross Margin %). Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

aov.intro: Average Order Value (AOV), worked end to end. The calculator takes Total Revenue, Total Orders; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
aov.outro: Average Order Value (AOV) settles it with AOV = Total Revenue ÷ Total Orders. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
aov.hi_intro: Average Order Value (AOV) ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Total Revenue aur Total Orders; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
aov.hi_outro: Average Order Value (AOV) ka formula: AOV = Total Revenue ÷ Total Orders. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

retention.intro: Repeat Rate, Retention & Churn, worked end to end. The calculator takes Customers (Start), Customers (End), New Customers Added; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
retention.outro: Repeat Rate, Retention & Churn settles it with Retention % = (Customers at End − New Customers) ÷ Customers at Start × 100; Churn % = 100 − Retention %. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
retention.hi_intro: Repeat Rate, Retention & Churn ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Customers (Start) aur Customers (End) aur New Customers Added; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
retention.hi_outro: Repeat Rate, Retention & Churn ka formula: Retention % = (Customers at End − New Customers) ÷ Customers at Start × 100; Churn % = 100 − Retention %. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

roas.intro: Return on Ad Spend (ROAS), worked end to end. The calculator takes Revenue from Ads, Ad Spend; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
roas.outro: Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) settles it with ROAS = Revenue from Ads ÷ Ad Spend. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
roas.hi_intro: Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Revenue from Ads aur Ad Spend; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
roas.hi_outro: Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) ka formula: ROAS = Revenue from Ads ÷ Ad Spend. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

funnel.intro: CPC, CPL, CPA & Conversion Rate, worked end to end. The calculator takes Ad Spend, Clicks, Leads, Conversions; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
funnel.outro: CPC, CPL, CPA & Conversion Rate settles it with CPC = Ad Spend ÷ Clicks. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
funnel.hi_intro: CPC, CPL, CPA & Conversion Rate ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Ad Spend aur Clicks aur Leads aur Conversions; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
funnel.hi_outro: CPC, CPL, CPA & Conversion Rate ka formula: CPC = Ad Spend ÷ Clicks. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

saas.intro: ARPU, MRR & ARR, worked end to end. The calculator takes Total Monthly Revenue, Active Users; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
saas.outro: ARPU, MRR & ARR settles it with MRR = Total Monthly Revenue from subscriptions. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
saas.hi_intro: ARPU, MRR & ARR ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Total Monthly Revenue aur Active Users; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
saas.hi_outro: ARPU, MRR & ARR ka formula: MRR = subscriptions se total monthly revenue. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

runrate.intro: Run Rate, worked end to end. The calculator takes Last Month's Revenue; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
runrate.outro: Run Rate settles it with Annual Run Rate = Last Month's Revenue × 12. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
runrate.hi_intro: Run Rate ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Last Month's Revenue; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
runrate.hi_outro: Run Rate ka formula: Annual Run Rate = Last Month's Revenue × 12. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

momyoy.intro: Month-on-Month / Year-on-Year Growth, worked end to end. The calculator takes Previous Value, Current Value; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
momyoy.outro: Month-on-Month / Year-on-Year Growth settles it with MoM % = (This Month - Last Month) / Last Month x 100. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
momyoy.hi_intro: Month-on-Month / Year-on-Year Growth ka poora hisaab. Tool leta hai Previous Value aur Current Value; neeche ek realistic set of numbers ke saath wahi ganit dikhaya gaya hai.
momyoy.hi_outro: Month-on-Month / Year-on-Year Growth ka formula: MoM % = (This Month - Last Month) / Last Month x 100. Koi bhi field badlo aur jawab turant badal jaata hai.

cagr.intro: CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate), worked end to end. The calculator takes Starting Value, Ending Value, Number of Years; the example below runs one realistic set of those numbers through it.
cagr.outro: CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) settles it with CAGR = (Ending Value ÷ Starting Value)^(1 ÷ Years) − 1. Change any field above and the answer updates with it.
